nodes.label: Existing Backend API Contracts
nodes.rationale: Existing backend APIs, data models, and authentication structures must not be changed; the Flutter app must conform to current API contracts, and needed backend changes must be flagged explicitly rather than implemented directly.

nodes.label: Flutter Mobile Agent
nodes.rationale: Agent role scoped exclusively to Flutter mobile development; must not modify backend APIs, data models, or auth structure, and must integrate with the existing ASP.NET Core 10 backend.

nodes.label: Development Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Ordered priorities: 1) preserve existing project architecture, 2) comply with existing backend API contract, 3) maintain Flutter code quality, 4) keep Web and Mobile behavior consistent, 5) avoid unnecessary changes.

nodes.label: Existing Project Architecture
nodes.rationale: Top priority: preserve the existing project architecture; analyze current structure before making changes and avoid redesigning code that is not yet understood.

nodes.label: Web and Mobile Behavioral Consistency
nodes.rationale: Common backend behavior between Web and Mobile should be treated as the baseline; platform-specific UI/UX should be applied in Flutter only where necessary, keeping business rules and user flows consistent across platforms.
